assumptions.title: Target Architecture Scope
assumptions.detail: Target landscape assumes SAP Integration Suite on SAP BTP with optional Edge Integration Cell for on-premise local execution.

assumptions.title: Automated Tooling Extraction
assumptions.detail: Assumes ~70% automated extraction feasibility for standard Small/Medium ICOs via SAP Migration Wizard; complex mappings require manual refactoring.

assumptions.title: Backend Remediation Exclusions
assumptions.detail: Excludes backend SAP ECC / S/4HANA ABAP custom code remediation, backend IDoc partner profile re-pointing, and network firewall provisioning.

assumptions.title: Blended Rate Delivery Model
assumptions.detail: Standard rate reflects a global delivery model (approx. 20% Onshore Architecture/Lead + 80% Offshore Build & QA).

toolingLimitations.title: ccBPM & Stateful Process Orchestration
toolingLimitations.limitation: The SAP Migration Assessment tool and Migration Wizard cannot automatically convert ccBPM or NetWeaver BPM processes.
toolingLimitations.technicalImpact: Stateful correlations, multi-step sync/async bridges, and long-running human workflows cannot execute in stateless Cloud Integration iFlows.
toolingLimitations.remediation: Decompose into stateless event-driven iFlows using SAP Event Mesh/JMS, or migrate human approval and multi-day stateful workflows to SAP Build Process Automation.

toolingLimitations.title: Custom Java Mappings & User-Defined Functions (UDFs)
toolingLimitations.limitation: Complex Java User-Defined Functions (Execution Type: All Values of Queue / Value Queue) and standalone Java mapping archives (.jar) are not auto-converted.
toolingLimitations.technicalImpact: Java mappings that rely on legacy NetWeaver runtime libraries (e.g., com.sap.aii.mapping.api) fail in Cloud Integration.
toolingLimitations.remediation: Rewrite Java logic into Groovy 3.x scripts. Groovy provides direct access to Camel Exchange headers, properties, and streaming XML/JSON parsers with significantly lower memory overhead.

toolingLimitations.title: Deprecated Adapters & Custom Adapter Modules
toolingLimitations.limitation: Legacy proprietary adapters (BC, CIDX, RNIF 1.1, MarketSet) and custom Java Enterprise Beans (EJB) adapter modules have no direct 1:1 runtime on SAP BTP.
toolingLimitations.technicalImpact: Pipelines relying on module chain modifications (e.g., custom payload compression, encryption, header injection) cannot be imported as-is.
toolingLimitations.remediation: Modernize communication protocols: replace RFC/SOAP with REST/OData APIs via SAP API Management, and replace custom EJB modules with modular Groovy script steps or pre-exit pipelines.

toolingLimitations.title: External Database & RFC Lookups in Mappings
toolingLimitations.limitation: Graphical message mappings containing synchronous JDBC or RFC lookups inside mapping iterations are flagged as high-risk performance bottlenecks.
toolingLimitations.technicalImpact: Executing round-trip database queries for each XML record across the Cloud Connector hybrid tunnel causes severe network latency and thread starvation.
toolingLimitations.remediation: Re-architect using Request-Reply or Content Enricher patterns before the mapping step, caching reference datasets into Cloud Integration memory or Global Variables.

toolingLimitations.title: Sync-to-Async / Async-to-Sync Bridges
toolingLimitations.limitation: Dual-stack Sync/Async bridges built on legacy ABAP Integration Engine pipelines do not translate to default Cloud Integration templates.
toolingLimitations.technicalImpact: Synchronous callers waiting on asynchronous backend responses can encounter connection timeouts if migrated as a single point-to-point iFlow.
toolingLimitations.remediation: Implement asynchronous decoupled patterns utilizing Cloud Integration JMS queues, or expose webhook-based callback endpoints to synchronous consumers.

decisionCriteria.question: Does data sovereignty or regulatory compliance mandate that payloads remain behind your firewall?
decisionCriteria.recommendation: Deploy Edge Integration Cell (On-Premise Kubernetes Runtime)
decisionCriteria.details: Edge Integration Cell keeps message execution completely on-premise while retaining centralized governance and design-time tooling on SAP BTP.

decisionCriteria.question: Are you processing high-volume ground-to-ground traffic between on-premise systems (e.g. Shop Floor / MES to ERP)?
decisionCriteria.details: Eliminates latency and internet egress charges by processing ground-to-ground traffic locally without hair-pinning payloads to the cloud.

decisionCriteria.question: Is your architecture cloud-first, connecting SaaS endpoints (Salesforce, Workday, Ariba, S/4HANA Cloud)?
decisionCriteria.recommendation: Adopt SAP Cloud Integration (Multi-Tenant BTP Runtime)
decisionCriteria.details: Fully managed multi-tenant runtime on SAP BTP with auto-scaling, elastic compute, automatic zero-downtime updates, and global reach.

decisionCriteria.question: Do you have existing on-premise SAP ECC or database systems that cloud apps must access securely?
decisionCriteria.recommendation: Deploy SAP Cloud Connector (Hybrid Inverted Tunnel)
decisionCriteria.details: Provides a reverse-proxy TLS tunnel requiring zero inbound ports opened in your corporate firewall, with full X.509 principal propagation.

startingSteps.title: Acquire SAP Integration Suite Entitlements
startingSteps.objective: Provision Cloud Integration runtime tenant and establish BTP subaccounts
startingSteps.prerequisites: SAP BTP Global Account with enterprise agreement (CPEA or Pay-As-You-Go)
startingSteps.businessOutcome: Standardized multi-tenant integration environment ready for developer onboarding and hybrid tunnel connectivity.
startingSteps.details: Request an SAP Integration Suite tenant in SAP BTP. Recommended edition for migration is Standard or Premium depending on throughput volume, Trading Partner Management (TPM) requirements, and Edge Integration Cell needs.
checklist: Provision SAP BTP Subaccount and assign Cloud Integration entitlements
Run the automated Integration Suite Booster in SAP BTP Cockpit
Configure custom Identity Provider (IAS) role collections for integration developers

startingSteps.title: Execute ISA-M Methodology Assessment
startingSteps.objective: Establish enterprise integration policy and style guide across cloud and on-premise
startingSteps.prerequisites: Enterprise architecture charter and catalog of existing business capabilities
startingSteps.businessOutcome: Documented integration guidelines preventing architecture sprawl and governing protocol standards.
startingSteps.details: Adopt SAP's Integration Solution Advisory Methodology (ISA-M) to classify integration domains (A2A, B2B, B2G, Event-Driven) and prescribe target architectural blueprints for development teams.
checklist: Define integration styles (Process, Data, B2B, User-centric, IoT/Event)
Formulate protocol governance: sunset legacy RFC/SOAP in favor of REST/OData APIs
Publish design guidelines for asynchronous queuing and exception handling

startingSteps.title: Establish Automated Regression Testing Strategy
startingSteps.objective: Implement automated payload comparison across legacy PO and target Cloud Integration
startingSteps.prerequisites: Sample production message archives and baseline test scripts
startingSteps.businessOutcome: Drastic reduction in business testing cycles with guaranteed payload parity and zero functional regressions.
startingSteps.details: Testing consumes 30–40% of migration effort. Establish regression tooling early (SAP Migration Wizard, Figaf, or Int4) to compare production PI/PO payloads against new Integration Suite iFlow outputs automatically.
checklist: Enable message payload persistence on key production PI/PO channels for test sample collection
Implement automated payload diff and schema comparison pipelines
Prepare unit and regression test suites for Wave 0 pilot interfaces

startingSteps.title: Upskill Integration Team to Cloud Integration & Groovy
startingSteps.objective: Train PI/PO architects and developers on Cloud Integration, Camel EIPs, and Groovy scripting
startingSteps.prerequisites: Assigned development resources and access to SAP Learning Hub
startingSteps.businessOutcome: Internal team self-sufficiency, eliminating costly long-term external contractor dependencies.
startingSteps.details: Transition legacy Java/ABAP integration skills to modern cloud patterns: Apache Camel Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIP), Groovy 3.x scripting, Cloud Integration Partner Directory, and Cloud ALM.
checklist: Complete SAP Learning Journey: Developing with SAP Integration Suite
Standardize Groovy reusable utility scripts for mapping, headers, and error handling
Review Enterprise Integration Patterns (Content-Based Router, Splitter, Aggregator)

startingSteps.title: Execute Self-Service Migration Assessment Tool
startingSteps.objective: Extract and analyze on-premise PI/PO ICO configurations and classify technical complexity
startingSteps.prerequisites: SAP Cloud Connector established with read-only extraction service user on PI/PO
startingSteps.businessOutcome: Objective, data-driven interface inventory classified into Small, Medium, Large, and Extra Large tiers.
startingSteps.details: Connect the SAP Migration Assessment tool in SAP BTP to your PI/PO system via SAP Cloud Connector. Extract Integrated Configuration Objects (ICOs), evaluate migration readiness, and generate automated effort reports.
checklist: Configure SAP Cloud Connector with access to PI/PO Directory and ESR APIs
Run data extraction in analysis mode across all active communication channels
Review generated PDF/Excel readiness reports to calibrate project T-shirt sizing

startingSteps.title: Inspect SAP Business Accelerator Hub for Pre-Delivered Packages
startingSteps.objective: Identify standard integration packages on api.sap.com to eliminate custom build effort
startingSteps.prerequisites: Catalog of connected third-party SaaS systems and target SAP applications
startingSteps.businessOutcome: 20–30% reduction in net build effort by adopting standard, vendor-supported integration content.
startingSteps.details: The SAP Business Accelerator Hub contains 3,500+ pre-built, production-ready integration packages for S/4HANA, Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow, Ariba, Concur, and government e-invoicing mandates.
checklist: Search api.sap.com for standard connectors to third-party endpoints
Evaluate pre-delivered SAP B2B Trading Partner packages for EDIFACT / X12
Adopt pre-built packages directly into your Cloud Integration tenant workspace

1.name: Discovery & Initiation
1.title: Phase 1: Discovery & Initiation
1.criticalRisk: Undocumented Legacy Interfaces & Outdated Routing Logic
1.riskMitigation: Execute automated discovery via ESR extraction; conduct functional stakeholder alignment to decommission zombie interfaces before sizing.
1.milestone: Landscape scope defined, project charter approved, stakeholder RACI signed off
1.description: Audit the current PI/PO footprint, document existing interfaces, confirm compliance boundaries, and align leadership on strategic business drivers.

checklist.text: Catalog current PI/PO landscape (Dual-stack vs Single-stack, NetWeaver 7.31/7.4/7.5)
checklist.sub: Record system IDs, active software components, and Basis kernel levels

checklist.text: Document all existing integration scenarios & communication channels
checklist.sub: Collect sender/receiver systems, protocols, custom adapters, and volume profiles

checklist.text: Define strategic business drivers and qualitative migration goals
checklist.sub: Map objectives against reduced TCO, cloud agility, scalability, and S/4HANA readiness

checklist.text: Establish Project RACI Matrix and sign-off accountability
checklist.sub: Ensure business process owners and functional leads are committed to testing waves

2.name: Migration Assessment
2.title: Phase 2: Migration Assessment
2.criticalRisk: Custom Java Mappings, Unsupported Adapters & ccBPM Dependencies
2.riskMitigation: Run SAP Migration Assessment tool; catalog custom Java archives and flag interfaces requiring complete Groovy refactoring or architectural redesign.
2.milestone: Assessment report generated, scenario complexity categorized, effort baseline approved
2.description: Run automated extraction against the SAP PI/PO Enterprise Services Repository (ESR) and Integration Directory (ID). Categorize each ICO by technical complexity and quantify development days.

checklist.text: Configure & run the SAP Migration Assessment Tool (or apply for SAP Migration Factory)
checklist.sub: Ensure Java runtime, configure Cloud Connector, and run data extractor in analysis mode

checklist.text: Analyze ICO readiness & classification
checklist.sub: Identify interfaces ready for automated extraction vs those requiring manual re-design

checklist.text: Generate scenario effort estimation report
checklist.sub: Audit breakdown: Async A2A, Sync A2A, B2B/EDI, BPM scenarios, and technical pass-throughs

checklist.text: Review custom components (Java UDFs, custom adapter modules, RFCs)
checklist.sub: Plan replacement with Groovy scripts, standard adapters, and modern REST/OData endpoints

3.name: Planning & Design
3.title: Phase 3: Planning & Design
3.criticalRisk: Complex Stateful Workflows & High-Throughput Ground-to-Ground Bottlenecks
3.riskMitigation: Formulate topology decision between pure Cloud Integration and Edge Integration Cell; redesign stateful flows into SAP Build Process Automation.
3.milestone: Target architecture blueprint approved, security posture established, templates finalized
3.description: Formulate the future-state cloud architecture. Determine whether pure cloud-native, Edge Integration Cell, or hybrid Cloud Connector is required, and establish standard iFlow patterns.

checklist.text: Score interface complexity using the 7-Factor Scoring Matrix
checklist.sub: Rate mapping complexity, routing rules, adapter types, security, volume, dependencies, error handling

checklist.text: Target Architecture Decision: Pure Cloud vs Hybrid vs Edge Integration Cell
checklist.sub: Analyze data sovereignty laws, latency sensitivity, and on-premise system accessibility

checklist.text: Design decoupled pipeline processing concept (EIP standards)
checklist.sub: Establish standardized inbound, routing, transformation, and outbound flow templates

checklist.text: Formulate ccBPM & BPM replacement strategy
checklist.sub: Transition long-running stateful workflows to SAP Build Process Automation or stateless iFlows

4.name: Wave Prioritization & Sizing
4.title: Phase 4: Wave Prioritization & Planning
4.criticalRisk: Business Criticality Alignment & Functional Team Capacity Bottlenecks
4.riskMitigation: Establish a Wave 0 non-critical pilot to prove hybrid connectivity and pipeline patterns; schedule high-risk waves around business peak seasons.
4.milestone: Wave schedule locked, team staffing onboarded, sprint backlog prioritized
4.description: Group interfaces into logical migration waves based on technical dependencies, business criticality, and early quick wins to build team confidence and validate operational readiness.

checklist.text: Apply 6-Factor Prioritization Model with weighted criteria
checklist.sub: Complexity (weight 5), Business Criticality (w=4), Dependencies (w=3), Volume (w=2), Resources (w=3), Quick Wins (w=4)

checklist.text: Sequence Wave 0 (Pilot / Non-Critical Quick Wins)
checklist.sub: Validate end-to-end deployment, Cloud Connector tunnel, and monitoring with low-risk interfaces

checklist.text: Establish team structure and FTE commitments
checklist.sub: Staff Program Manager, Integration Architect, Integration Developers, Test Leads, and Basis Admins

checklist.text: Check SAP Business Accelerator Hub for pre-built packages
checklist.sub: Save 20-30% development effort by adopting standard pre-delivered SAP content

5.name: Execution & Testing
5.title: Phase 5: Execution & Testing
5.criticalRisk: Cross-System Regression, Partner Coordinate Latency & Payload Discrepancies
5.riskMitigation: Mandate automated three-tier testing (UT, IT, UAT) with payload diff comparisons; establish early engagement with external B2B trading partners.
5.milestone: Development complete, unit testing certified, regression & UAT sign-off obtained
5.description: Execute the core build and testing cycle for each wave following the 6-step wave execution sequence and three-tier testing strategy.

checklist.text: Step 1: Develop new iFlows (or auto-convert via Migration Toolkit)
checklist.sub: Import ICOs into Cloud Integration package; review generated flows and routing condition logic

checklist.text: Step 2: Configure communication adapters & credential artifacts
checklist.sub: Setup Cloud Connector mappings, certificates, endpoint URLs, and authentication aliases

checklist.text: Step 3: Map data transformations & migrate custom logic
checklist.sub: Import ESR message mappings; rewrite legacy Java User-Defined Functions (UDFs) to Groovy

checklist.text: Step 4: Execute Three-Tier Testing Strategy (UT, IT, UAT)
checklist.sub: Validate individual components, cross-system integration, and obtain business sign-off

6.name: Cutover & Hypercare
6.title: Phase 6: Cutover & Hypercare
6.criticalRisk: Unplanned Downtime & In-Flight Message Loss During Live Switchover
6.riskMitigation: Execute rigid queue draining protocol; lock PI communication channels and verify zero pending messages in SMQ1/SMQ2 before redirecting DNS/endpoints.
6.milestone: PI/PO interfaces decommissioned, IS flows productive, hypercare transitioned to BAU
6.description: Transition traffic smoothly to SAP Integration Suite with zero unplanned downtime. Execute the cutover checklist, manage parallel runs where applicable, and maintain 24/7 hypercare support.

checklist.text: Verify technical prerequisites (tenants provisioned, security deployed, certs valid)
checklist.sub: All target Cloud Integration packages deployed and showing 'Started' status

checklist.text: Execute connectivity sanity tests with all external endpoints
checklist.sub: Confirm ping and handshake with B2B partners, cloud apps, and on-premise SAP systems

checklist.text: Cutover window: Stop PI/PO sender communication channels & drain queues
checklist.sub: Ensure zero messages stuck in PI queues (SMQ1/SMQ2) before channel redirection

checklist.text: Activate SAP Integration Suite endpoints & redirect traffic
checklist.sub: Update DNS, firewall rules, or partner webhook URLs to point to new cloud endpoints

challenges.title: 1. Loss of Tribal Knowledge & Undocumented Custom Logic
challenges.desc: PI/PO systems running for 10–15 years have accumulated complex graphical mappings with embedded Java UDFs whose original authors have left the organization.
challenges.mitigation: Run automated metadata extraction with SAP Migration Assessment tool. Isolate all custom Java UDFs and conduct structured reverse-engineering workshops with functional owners.

challenges.title: 2. High Testing Burden Across Connected Systems
challenges.desc: Integration testing often represents 40–50% of total project effort. Co-ordinating with dozens of third-party vendors and internal application teams creates scheduling bottlenecks.
challenges.mitigation: Adopt automated testing accelerators (SAP Migration Wizard, Figaf, or Int4) that capture live production PI/PO payloads and execute automated regression assertions against Integration Suite.

challenges.title: 3. ccBPM & Stateful Process Dependencies
challenges.desc: Cross-Component BPM (ccBPM) or NetWeaver BPM orchestrations containing stateful correlations, multicasters, and human approvals cannot be auto-migrated to stateless iFlows.
challenges.mitigation: Architecturally decouple business logic: migrate human tasks and stateful processes to SAP Build Process Automation, while converting pure integration steps to decoupled, event-driven iFlows.

challenges.title: 4. Deprecated Adapters & Unsupported Protocols
challenges.desc: Legacy interfaces utilizing deprecated adapters (BC, CIDX, RNIF, or custom adapter modules) require protocol modernization.
challenges.mitigation: Transition to modern REST/OData APIs managed through SAP API Management, or leverage SAP Integration Advisor (MIGs/MAGs) for standardized B2B/EDI protocols.

recommendations.sub: Begin with 5–10 simple, non-critical point-to-point interfaces to validate the end-to-end delivery pipeline and hybrid connectivity.
Audit interface traffic logs in PI/PO. On average, 15–25% of interfaces have had zero traffic in the past 12 months and should be retired rather than migrated.
Before building custom iFlows, check the SAP Business Accelerator Hub (api.sap.com). Standard packages save 20–30% in development effort.
Implement an enterprise Integration Architecture Guide (ISA-M) with standardized templates for error handling, logging, and routing.
Deploy automated testing tools to compare production PI/PO message payloads with Cloud Integration outputs to compress UAT cycles.
Train internal developers on Apache Camel Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIP), Groovy scripting, and SAP Cloud ALM before starting complex waves.
Utilize SAP Integration Advisor crowdsourced ML to accelerate EDIFACT and ANSI X12 mapping generation by up to 60%.

recommendations.text: Deploy SAP Cloud ALM for Monitoring
recommendations.sub: Implement SAP Cloud ALM alongside Cloud Integration from Day 1 for centralized end-to-end message tracking and proactive alerting.
Establish clear cutover playbooks with queue-draining procedures, rollback plans, and temporary parallel runs for high-criticality flows.
Take advantage of SAP's complimentary 2–3 week assessment service to gain official validation on interface inventory and complexity sizing.
